start.title: Who benefits from the ban?
start.line: Cigarette ads get banned. Bad news for cigarette companies… or could it help them?
dialogue: Cigarette ads get banned. Bad news for cigarette companies… or could it help them?

expect_harm.title: Investigate the same question
expect_harm.line: That’s a reasonable guess. But their competitors lose ads too. Let’s investigate what that changes.
dialogue: That’s a reasonable guess. But their competitors lose ads too. Let’s investigate what that changes.

expect_help.title: Investigate the same question
expect_help.line: Maybe. Let’s investigate how losing the same option could help competitors.
dialogue: Maybe. Let’s investigate how losing the same option could help competitors.

expect_unsure.title: Investigate the same question
expect_unsure.line: Let’s investigate. We’ll compare one company stopping with both companies stopping.
dialogue: Let’s investigate. We’ll compare one company stopping with both companies stopping.

baseline.title: Before either stops
baseline.line: Two rivals. The same customers. Let’s follow one day’s money.
dialogue: Two rivals. The same customers. Let’s follow one day’s money.

visual.phase: Before the ban · two fictional competitors
visual.rule: A and B compete for the same customers.

alone.title: Only A stops
alone.line: A keeps less: 40. Its ad bill vanished—but customers paid B instead.
dialogue: A keeps less: 40. Its ad bill vanished—but customers paid B instead.

visual.phase: Fictional comparison · Company A and Company B
visual.rule: Same total spending. Ads change who gets the customers.
visual.receipt: A receives 40 − spends 0 on ads = 40 left

both_after_alone.title: B stops too
both_after_alone.line: Back to 100! Customers split evenly again. This time, neither company has an ad bill.
dialogue: Back to 100! Customers split evenly again. This time, neither company has an ad bill.

visual.phase: Fictional comparison · Company A and Company B
visual.rule: Same total spending. Ads change who gets the customers.
visual.receipt: A receives 100 − spends 0 on ads = 100 left

together.title: Both stop
together.line: Both stop. No ad bills. Now try letting only B advertise.
dialogue: Both stop. No ad bills. Now try letting only B advertise.

visual.phase: Fictional comparison · Company A and Company B
visual.rule: Same total spending. Ads change who gets the customers.
visual.receipt: A receives 100 − spends 0 on ads = 100 left

alone_after_both.title: B can advertise again
alone_after_both.line: B’s ads return. Watch the customers—and their payments—shift.
dialogue: B’s ads return. Watch the customers—and their payments—shift.

visual.phase: Fictional comparison · Company A and Company B
visual.rule: Same total spending. Ads change who gets the customers.
visual.receipt: A receives 40 − spends 0 on ads = 40 left

compare.title: One change explains the difference
compare.line: A’s ads are off in both pictures. What changed its money?
dialogue: A’s ads are off in both pictures. What changed its money?

visual.caption: Same company · same choice · different competitor action

choices.label: A saves its ad bill only once

clarify.title: A saved its bill in both tests
clarify.line: A pays zero for ads in both. The difference is whether B can still advertise.
dialogue: A pays zero for ads in both. The difference is whether B can still advertise.

concept.title: Strategic interdependence
concept.line: A’s result depends on B’s choice too. That’s strategic interdependence. Looking at A alone misses half the story.
dialogue: A’s result depends on B’s choice too. That’s strategic interdependence. Looking at A alone misses half the story.

resolve.title: Return to the opening question
resolve.line: Yes, it could. Stopping together can help where stopping alone hurts. Our example shows how—not what the real companies earned.
dialogue: Yes, it could. Stopping together can help where stopping alone hurts. Our example shows how—not what the real companies earned.

visual.phase: Fictional comparison · Company A and Company B
visual.rule: Same total spending. Ads change who gets the customers.
visual.receipt: A receives 100 − spends 0 on ads = 100 left

choices.label: What did the real evidence show?

evidence.title: The real case
evidence.line: Stock-market evidence suggested investors expected established tobacco companies to benefit. Harder entry for new brands was another possible reason.
dialogue: Stock-market evidence suggested investors expected established tobacco companies to benefit. Harder entry for new brands was another possible reason.

entry.title: Recognition matters
entry.line: Established brands were already familiar. New brands lost a way to get noticed. Other advertising channels remained.
dialogue: Established brands were already familiar. New brands lost a way to get noticed. Other advertising channels remained.

limit.title: The assumption matters
limit.line: Our example held total spending fixed. If customers bought much less, lost income could outweigh the saved ad bills.
dialogue: Our example held total spending fixed. If customers bought much less, lost income could outweigh the saved ad bills.

starting_money.title: They start in the same position
starting_money.line: Only A stops its ads. B keeps advertising. Will A keep more or less than its current 60 coins?
dialogue: Only A stops its ads. B keeps advertising. Will A keep more or less than its current 60 coins?

visual.rule: Total spending stays fixed in this example.

ban_arrives.title: The ban arrives
ban_arrives.line: Now B must stop advertising too. Will A’s money recover?
dialogue: Now B must stop advertising too. Will A’s money recover?

visual.phase: Fictional comparison · Company A and Company B
visual.rule: Same total spending. Ads change who gets the customers.
visual.receipt: A receives 40 − spends 0 on ads = 40 left
